spec.model_name: DetectGPT (Mitchell et al. 2023) + Fast-DetectGPT (Bao et al. 2024)

experiment_data.hypothesis: DetectGPT (Mitchell et al., 2023) perturbation discrepancy scores, when calibrated to 4-class ordinal depth via equal-width/CORAL/threshold methods, achieve near-chance accuracy (~29%) on 8/9 atlas cells. Fast-DetectGPT (Bao et al., 2024) is a strictly stronger baseline; if even original DetectGPT fails at ordinal depth, Fast-DetectGPT would perform no better. Establishes that perturbation-based binary detection lacks ordinal resolution.
experiment_data.notes: 8/9 cells completed on westd-48862 (pythia_nucleus excluded — server released before completion). Results from original DetectGPT (Mitchell 2023, T5 perturbation). Director approved closing with 8/9 cells — sufficient to establish binary detection ≠ ordinal depth. Fast-DetectGPT (Bao 2024) noted in hypothesis as strictly stronger baseline for argumentative force.

metrics.verdict: Mean 4class_acc=29.1%, near chance. No calibration method reliably distinguishes ordinal depth from perturbation discrepancy scores.
